meta.important_question: Will the city canvassing board certify the race on the ordinary near-term timetable without a major procedural delay?

realization_criteria: certification occurs without extraordinary postponement beyond ordinary local process window
no unresolved delayed-precinct tabulation defect blocks certification

blockers: high switching costs for losing campaign

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Informal demands for recount do not realize this endpoint unless a formal mechanism is triggered.

meta.important_question: Will a campaign or authorized body initiate a formal recount or equivalent challenge tied to the delayed precincts?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly names recount demand as a major branch.
realization_criteria: campaign files recount request or formal contest
city_canvassing_board or other competent body schedules challenge-related review
public reporting confirms formal procedural escalation beyond informal allegation
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: One campaign has already alleged selective delays, creating a clear path to formal escalation if margin or narrative incentives support it.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Persistent doubt can coexist with timely certification and even with absence of recount.
endpoint_ledger.description: A durable segment of the public continues to treat the result as suspicious even after count completion or certification.
endpoint_ledger.label: Persistent Legitimacy Doubt

meta.important_question: After counting is completed, will rumor-driven doubts about legitimacy remain materially active in public discourse?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Misinformation persistence is explicitly named and may be more consequential than any single procedural move.
realization_criteria: continued rumor or suspicion narratives remain salient after official count completion
multiple public channels show recurring doubt claims detached from new evidence
trust in city_election_office among key skeptical cohorts remains materially depressed relative to T0
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Rumor spread and strategic allegations are already present at initialization, creating a path for persistent doubt even without formal contest success.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Legitimacy repair does not require universal trust, only broad enough acceptance to reduce active contestation.
endpoint_ledger.description: Public confidence recovers enough that the outage is broadly treated as an administratively resolved disruption rather than evidence of selective manipulation.
endpoint_ledger.label: Legitimacy Repair

meta.important_question: Will official transparency and civic patience messaging restore enough confidence to prevent broad escalation of contestation?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly instructs initialization around legitimacy repair as a possible outcome.
realization_criteria: official explanation and paper-ballot verification are broadly repeated without major contradiction
rumor volume declines across local social and press channels
affected precinct voters show visible acceptance that ballots were counted and safeguarded
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: There is credible repair capacity because paper ballots are secure and civic groups are already advocating patience, but trust is not yet stabilized.

Localized delays plus anecdotal influencer content create favorable conditions for durable suspicion before official clarity arrives.
Formal endpoint progression depends on election office processing and canvassing board certification authority.
If the delayed precincts are decisive, conflict and recount pressure could intensify sharply, but margin evidence is absent at T0.
Some trust-leaning residents may stay quiet, allowing more skeptical narratives to appear dominant in public channels.

simulation_brief.scope: fictional city-level election administration and public discourse
simulation_brief.summary: A fictional city council race faces uncertainty after a ballot-scanner outage delays results in three precincts. Paper ballots are reportedly secure, but the delay creates room for allegations of selective treatment, rumor spread, recount pressure, and competing narratives about legitimacy. T0 should center on trust, uncertainty, legal authority, rumor dynamics, and branching possibilities around certification, recount demands, misinformation persistence, and legitimacy repair.
uncertainty_notes: Cause and duration of scanner outage are not specified beyond delay.
No evidence establishes fraud, tampering, or final margin at T0.
Scale of influencer reach and campaign capacity is inferred as local, not citywide mass dominance.
Legal procedures for recount/certification are implied but not fully described in source text.

sociology_baseline.note: Residents accept updates mostly from moderately trusted institutions, civic groups, or aligned campaigns.
Mobilization likely rises if recount language, legal action, or contradictory updates appear.
Many privately trust the process more than they publicly express during uncertainty.
Interpretations cluster by political and media network ties.
Rumor acceptance increases when repeated by campaign-adjacent and influencer sources together.
People read outage narratives through side loyalty and place-based fairness concerns.
If no new controversy emerges, some public attention can soften over time.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Technical outage delays results, but paper ballots are reported secure, creating a contest between procedural reassurance and suspicion.
A campaign introduces fairness-based suspicion without established proof, increasing ambiguity rather than certainty.
Civic groups provide a de-escalatory frame that can compete with outrage narratives if amplified.
Precinct-level anecdotes and local influencer posts are likely to personalize and intensify uncertainty.
Formal legitimacy depends on a certifying body downstream from election administration.
